items.name: narration_en
items.direction: Narrate this for a premium documentary YouTube Shorts channel about money, history and the tricks behind them. The Narrator is a deep, warm, confident storyteller with a hint of mystery: curious, quietly amused, energetic and punchy, never slow, never announcer-like. Natural emphasis on dates and numbers, questions end with a curious lift, a short comic pause before each punchline. Keep the same voice, pace and energy from start to finish. Chars voices two funny cartoon characters (a smug gold bar and a nervous banknote), short and punchy, performed exactly as described in each bracket.
lines: Your gold necklace can lose two hundred dollars the moment you pay. Gold didn't fall. So what did?
Next week is Dhanteras, India's biggest day for buying gold.
[smug, deep, rich gold bar, very pleased with himself] My favourite holiday. Obviously.
But a thousand dollar necklace isn't a thousand dollars of gold.
So what are you really paying for?
Making charges: the fee for design and labour. On necklaces, often twenty percent or more.
When you sell, most jewellers pay only for the gold inside.
And that's still not the worst part.
The making charges? Gone. The tax? Gone.
That's the mirage: you thought you bought gold. Part of your money bought art.
So a thousand dollar necklace can sell back for around eight hundred dollars, even if gold never moves.
Many savers pick coins or bars instead.
[delighted, squeaky banknote, surprised to be winning] Gold losing value? Best day ever!
Comment: do you buy gold to wear or save?
This is Money Mirage. Follow for more.
